steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, but shorter wavelengths like blue are scattered roughly 10 times more than longer wavelengths like red, causing blue light to be dispersed in all directions across the sky. Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are less sensitive to violet and some of it is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so the sky ultimately looks blue to us.
